concerns.text: The 'clean finite-time baseline' used to compute the deviation Δλ is derived from a single noise‑free trajectory per system dimension (N). This provides no estimate of baseline variability, yet Δλ is defined as the difference from this single value. If the baseline itself fluctuates across runs, the deviation metric inherits that noise, biasing the regression analysis and violating the independence of the validation target from the predictor (noise level). A robust approach should compute multiple clean baselines per N and propagate their variance into Δλ.

SC‑001 validates numerical stability by measuring convergence of the clean‑system FTLE to the asymptotic baseline using the same integration routine and tolerances as the noisy analysis. Because the same algorithmic pipeline is used for both the predictor (clean baseline) and the outcome (FTLE bias), the validation is not truly independent; systematic integration bias could be mistaken for genuine numerical stability, leading to circular validation of the metric.
